summary: ORBITAL is an interactive space mission simulation game that challenges players to take on the role of a mission commander responsible for planning, managing, and successfully completing a 24-month journey to Mars. The game combines space exploration, strategic resource management, scientific decision-making, and skill-based mini-games to create an educational and engaging gaming experience. Players must design their spacecraft within a limited budget and weight capacity, manage essential resources such as oxygen, power, and crew morale, and respond to unexpected challenges throughout the mission. As the mission progresses, players encounter various space-related emergencies and operational challenges that require quick thinking, problem-solving, and effective decision-making. Each decision can directly influence the spacecraft's condition, crew survival, and overall mission success. The ultimate objective is to reach Mars within 24 months while maintaining sufficient resources, keeping the crew alive, and achieving a minimum science score of 30%.
details:
Designing and Managing a Mission to Mars

ORBITAL is a browser-based educational game prototype developed to introduce players to the fundamentals of space mission design through an interactive Mars science mission. Players take on the responsibilities of spacecraft designers and mission operators, making decisions that determine whether their mission can successfully reach its objectives.

The experience begins with spacecraft configuration, where players select different components while working within a limited construction budget and rocket lifting capacity. Once the spacecraft is prepared, players launch their mission and manage its resources, crew conditions, and scientific progress throughout a simulated 24-month mission.

The central concept behind ORBITAL is that successful space missions require careful planning and engineering trade-offs. Every spacecraft component has different advantages, costs, and limitations. Players must understand how their decisions influence the overall performance and sustainability of their mission.

Spacecraft Design and Configuration

Players begin with a 100-point construction budget and must select suitable equipment for their spacecraft. The available categories include:

  • Rocket Selection: Choose between Small, Medium, and Big rockets, each with different lifting capacities.
  • Solar Power Systems: Select solar panels to determine the spacecraft's starting power and monthly power consumption.
  • Air Systems: Choose between a Basic Air Filter, Air Recycler, and Closed-Loop System to manage breathable air.
  • Communication Systems: Select radio equipment, including Basic Radio, Big Dish, and Deep-Space Array.
  • Mission Equipment: Choose between All-Rounder, Safety Kit, and Science Lab configurations.

Each selection affects the spacecraft's mass, construction budget, and starting resources. The game includes a live spacecraft preview that updates according to the player's choices, allowing them to compare different configurations before launch.

Mission Operations and Resource Management

After launch, players must manage their spacecraft and crew throughout 24 monthly mission turns. The main resources monitored during operations include:

  • Science: Represents the scientific progress and research output of the mission.
  • Power: Represents the electrical energy available for spacecraft operations.
  • Air: Represents the available breathable air supporting the crew.
  • Morale: Represents the condition and morale of the crew.

Players must maintain sufficient resources while responding to different mission situations. Poor decisions or insufficient resources can threaten the survival of the crew and lead to mission failure.

Random Mission Events and Emergency Challenges

During the mission, players encounter different events involving spacecraft hazards, technical repairs, crew situations, and scientific opportunities.

These events introduce uncertainty into the gameplay and require players to evaluate possible responses. Certain decisions activate interactive minigames, making mission operations more engaging while testing players' ability to react to unexpected situations.

Interactive Minigames

ORBITAL incorporates 24 short minigame types inspired by different spacecraft and mission-operation activities.

Examples include:

  • Wire matching and electrical connections.
  • Grid repair and system troubleshooting.
  • Sequence memory challenges.
  • Lander control activities.
  • Solar energy collection.
  • Orbit-related tasks.
  • Scientific analysis activities.

These interactive challenges allow players to experience simplified mission-related tasks while making the overall learning experience more engaging.

Multiple Difficulty Modes and Competition

To accommodate different experience levels, ORBITAL includes four gameplay modes:

  • Tutorial Mode
  • Cadet Mode
  • Commander Mode
  • Ranked Hardcore Mode

Each mode introduces different levels of difficulty, crew sizes, starting resources, and event penalties.

The game also includes a leaderboard system for ranked scores, encouraging replayability and competition between players. Players can review their mission outcomes through the Report, Crew, Leaderboard, and Export sections.

A mission is considered successful when the player completes the 24-month mission with at least 30 Science while keeping the crew and critical resources operational. At the end of the mission, players receive a final grade and mission report summarizing their performance.

Technical Development and Innovation

ORBITAL is developed as a browser-based game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Its interface combines a science-fiction-inspired visual design with interactive spacecraft previews, mission-control dashboards, resource indicators, event systems, and minigame interfaces.

The spacecraft configuration system uses JavaScript rules to calculate the effects of equipment selections on the construction budget, spacecraft mass, and starting resources. During mission operations, authored event tables, difficulty settings, and resource-management rules determine the progression of the simulation.

The project also incorporates Firebase Firestore to support its ranked leaderboard functionality, allowing eligible players to submit and compare their mission scores.

The creativity behind ORBITAL lies in combining simplified systems engineering with interactive gameplay. Instead of simply presenting information about space exploration, the game allows players to experience how different engineering choices can influence the outcome of a mission.

Through this approach, ORBITAL aims to make space mission design more accessible to teenagers, students, and beginners interested in aerospace engineering and planetary exploration.
